question.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $L?$

I. $L∨(¬M∧L)$

II. $(L∧¬M)∨L$

III. $(¬M∧L)∨L$
question.worked_solution:
The law that disjunction absorbs conjunction is stated as

$$
L∨(L∧¬M)≡L.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is logically equivalent to $L.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}L∨(¬M∧L) & ≡L∨(L∧¬M) \\  & ≡L.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is logically equivalent to $L.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(L∧¬M)∨L & ≡L∨(L∧¬M) \\  & ≡L.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $L.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(¬M∧L)∨L & ≡L∨(¬M∧L) \\  & ≡L∨(L∧¬M) \\  & ≡L.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."
